name: GPU Mesh Voxelization via Axis-Aligned Projection
aliases: GPU Voxelization via Rasterization and Geometry Shader Axis Projection
GPU Mesh Voxelization via Axis-Aligned Projection — Dominant Axis Projection
definition: A GPU-based voxelization technique that converts triangle meshes into a 3D voxel grid. It uses a geometry shader to determine the dominant axis of each triangle's normal and projects the triangle onto the corresponding 2D plane (X, Y, or Z) to write voxel data into a 3D texture or structured buffer.
summary: GPU Mesh Voxelization via Axis-Aligned Projection converts triangle meshes to 3D voxel grids by projecting each triangle onto its dominant normal axis, minimizing gaps and leveraging hardware rasterization.
